lead_with.title: Agentic commerce is a US story
lead_with.text: The agentic-commerce wave (AI agents that search and buy) is being driven by US platforms and payment networks. KEYBAN's **Agent Wallet** fits that conversation better than the EU-only Digital Product Passport angle.

person.name: Nenad Cetkovic
person.text: Nenad is **COO and co-founder** of KEYBAN (title from Streak and his email signature). Frenchweb describes him as bringing **e-commerce experience, including at Lengow**. On the Sep 22 call he explained his caution about the US, linked to the **Lengow US experience** (details **to be confirmed**). He plans to go to the US **after** KEYBAN's next fundraise. He writes in French and is formal but friendly; he rescheduled once (Sep 17) and confirmed quickly. He travels to tech events (VivaTech 2026, Silicon Summit, Web Summit). Earlier career and education are not verified.

company.text: KEYBAN was founded in **2024** in Paris. It sells a **blockchain-based SaaS / API platform** that turns user accounts into wallets and products into digital assets. Three building blocks: **Digital Product Passports** (certified product data for the EU DPP rules), **programmable loyalty**, and an **Agent Wallet** so AI agents can pay and subscribe on behalf of buyers. It targets **retail, e-commerce, luxury and art**. The March 2026 release says clients include large French banks, big retail brands, listed companies and art-sector organizations (**none named**). SaaS and commerce-platform plugins were announced for the following quarter. Co-founder and CEO **Charles Kremer** is a blockchain specialist. KEYBAN was a Business France exhibitor at **VivaTech 2026**.

financials.text: No public accounts found. **Funding:** seed round with business angels including Jean-Marc Bouhelier and Jean-Christophe Personnat (Frenchweb), then a **€500K pre-seed** from existing shareholders announced **Mar 17, 2026**. **Revenue:** **>€1M** and self-funded, as Nenad said on the Sep 22 call (Olivier's recap); not publicly verified. A larger fundraise is being prepared (amount and timing **to be confirmed**). Team size **to be confirmed**.

history.text: Johanna T booked the first call from LinkedIn on **Sep 16**. Nenad moved it on **Sep 17**; Olivier rescheduled to **Sep 22** and Nenad confirmed. The call took place **Sep 22, 2026**. Same day, Olivier sent a recap: start in **January**, build traction during the raise, fix social credibility, program = **10 qualified meetings a month** for **$3,400/month** (no long-term contract, one-month notice, 3-month minimum), 3 pillars Promote / Network / Engage, plus the 2-min and 9-min videos for Nenad and Charles. Nenad replied: "Je regarde tout cela et on se reparle comme convenu." On **Oct 18** Olivier sent the new-website email (opened once, no reply). Follow-up call booked for **Dec 8, 2026**; a Streak task is due Dec 7.

industry.title: Agentic commerce is taking off
industry.text: AI agents that search, compare and buy are a fast-growing topic in 2026; wallets and payment rails for agents are the infrastructure layer. KEYBAN positions itself there.

industry.title: EU Digital Product Passport
industry.text: The EU DPP rules push brands to certify product data. This is a European driver; in the US the hook is traceability, authenticity and loyalty instead.

industry.title: Luxury and resale authentication
industry.text: US resale and luxury players use digital IDs for authenticity. A natural US use case for product passports (**to be confirmed** with Nenad which verticals he sees in the US).

industry.title: Crowded wallet space
industry.text: Many wallet and tokenization start-ups compete. US buyers will ask what is different; KEYBAN needs a crisp one-line answer.

talking_points: What came out of Silicon Summit and Web Summit: which US companies or buyer types showed real interest?
Where are you on the fundraise: target amount, timing, and do investors ask about US traction?
Which US buyer do you want first: retail brands, e-commerce platforms, luxury, or payment players?
Who signs off on the US budget: you, Charles, or the board?
What happened at Lengow in the US, and what would you do differently this time?
Can we agree on a January start so you have Q1 meetings to show investors?

attention.title: US timing objection
attention.text: He wants to wait until after the raise. Expect him to repeat it; answer with the traction-for-valuation argument.

attention.title: Two decision-makers
attention.text: CEO **Charles Kremer** must be convinced too. Ask whether Charles watched the videos and invite him to the Dec 8 call or a follow-up.

attention.title: Revenue not verified
attention.text: The >€1M figure comes from the call, not public filings. Do not quote it back as a public fact.

attention.title: Small budget
attention.text: €500K pre-seed means $3,400/month is a real line item. Frame it against the value of a stronger fundraise.
